quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
You should always brake hard to make sure you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Press the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Come to a complete stop, check for traffic, and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, check for traffic, and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: When the road is wet, slow down.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic is increasing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that wet roads are slippery and they should reduce speed.

questions.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: Driving slower than surrounding traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: How do defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to respond to them.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at accidents or unusual events:

options.text: Causes traffic to back up.
Prevents rear-end collisions.
Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic to back up.
questions.explanation: Avoid looking at accidents or unusual events while driving. This practice reduces traffic congestion.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is a distraction because:

options.text: It makes the driver worry about the cost of the call.
It uses the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
It draws the attention of other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It uses the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Cell phones are dangerous while driving because they use your eyes, hands, and mind. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk by using a phone on the road.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic stays in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes without signaling.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes left or right. Stay in the right lane if you are going slower than traffic around you. It is illegal to back up or make a U-turn on interstate highways. If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled in. Even after the bus moves, do not go until you are sure no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. This sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes you to take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is the most common cause of traffic accidents. Any distraction causes drivers to miss important sights and sounds needed to avoid crashes.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane if you:

options.text: Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: See the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane after passing, make sure you are not too close to the car you just passed. When you can see both headlights of the vehicle in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return to your lane.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with flashing red lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students get off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped. Wait until the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus begins to move.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly or without planning.
Check for other vehicles entering the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly or without planning.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in the space you want to enter. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes to give other drivers time to react.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn in that direction after slowing down and checking traffic.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
May turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means "stop." You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: To help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up when entering curves and slow down when exiting them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may be merging into your lane ahead.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead of your vehicle:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
Allows you to spot police officers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead to avoid sudden braking or turning. By looking ahead and being ready to stop or change lanes, you can drive safely, save fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is necessary to react properly to things you see or hear while driving. Even if you are below the legal blood alcohol limit, any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on each side. Avoid driving beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents your car from veering into oncoming traffic if hit from behind. When parked on a slope, turn wheels so the car will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When passing a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You may turn in that direction after a complete stop.
You may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means traffic in that lane cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal to proceed.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, give the right-of-way to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who arrived before you.
Across from your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: After stopping, vehicles should go through in the order they arrived. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: Always stop before railroad tracks when:

options.text: There is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to fully cross.
The crossing is in a city with frequent train traffic.
You are transporting two or more children.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to fully cross.
questions.explanation: Expect trains on any track at any time. Do not cross if you cannot completely clear the tracks before stopping. Make sure your vehicle fully clears the tracks.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid line and a dashed line, only drivers next to the dashed line may cross to pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: In traffic moving at 50 to 55 mph, you have the least chance of an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to other traffic on the road (within posted limits). Vehicles moving at the same speed cannot hit each other. Crashes often happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.
